'''Alexey Pokrovskiy''' is a mathematician specialising in [[combinatorics]] and [[graph theory]]. He is an associate professor in the Department of Mathematics at [[University College London]].<ref name="ucl-profile">{{cite web |title=Alexey Pokrovskiy |url=https://profiles.ucl.ac.uk/78145-alexey-pokrovskiy |publisher=University College London |access-date=3 May 2026}}</ref><ref name="ucl-staff">{{cite web |title=Academic and Lecturing Staff |url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/mathematical-physical-sciences/maths/people/academic-and-lecturing-staff |publisher=University College London |access-date=3 May 2026}}</ref> He is known for his work in [[Extremal combinatorics|extremal]] and [[Combinatorics|probabilistic combinatorics]], including a proof of [[Graceful labeling|Ringel’s conjecture]] with [[Richard Montgomery (mathematician)|Richard Montgomery]] and [[Benny Sudakov]] for large graphs, as covered by [[Quanta Magazine|Quanta magazine.]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hartnett |first=Kevin |date=2020-02-19 |title=Rainbow Proof Shows Graphs Have Uniform Parts |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/mathematicians-prove-ringels-graph-theory-conjecture-20200219/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref> In 2019, he and Montgomery received the [[European Prize in Combinatorics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BEI Research Year in Review {{!}} Birkbeck Research Blog |url=https://research.blogs.bbk.ac.uk/2020/01/07/bei-research-year-in-review/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=research.blogs.bbk.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Birmingham Researcher Receives European Prize in Combinatorics |url=https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/university/colleges/eps/news/2019/10/researcher-receives-prize-combinatorics.aspx |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=University of Birmingham |language=en}}</ref>

== Education and career ==

Pokrovskiy studied mathematics at the [[University of Cambridge]], receiving a BA in 2008 and an MMath with distinction in 2009. He completed a PhD in mathematics at the [[London School of Economics]] in 2013 under the supervision of Jan van den Heuvel and Jozef Skokan.<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Pokrovskiy |first=Alexey |title=Graph powers, partitions, and other extremal problems |date=May 2013|degree=doctoral |publisher=London School of Economics and Political Science |url=https://researchonline.lse.ac.uk/id/eprint/131782/ |language=en}}</ref>

Pokrovskiy was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Free University of Berlin]] from 2013 to 2015 and at [[ETH Zurich]] from 2015 to 2018. He was then a lecturer at [[Birkbeck, University of London]] from 2018 to 2020, before joining [[University College London]] in 2020.<ref name="cv">{{cite web |title=Curriculum vitae |url=https://alexeypokrovskiy.com/cv.pdf |first=Alexey |last=Pokrovskiy |access-date=3 May 2026}}</ref><ref name="ucl-newsletter">{{cite web |title=De Morgan Association Newsletter 2019 |url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/mathematical-physical-sciences/sites/mathematical_physical_sciences/files/demorgan_newsletter_2019.pdf |publisher=University College London |access-date=3 May 2026}}</ref>

== Research ==

Pokrovskiy's work is in discrete mathematics, especially extremal and probabilistic combinatorics. His notable results include an approximate version of the [[Ron Aharoni|Aharoni]]-Berger conjecture and his work with Matija Bucić, Matthew Kwan and [[Benny Sudakov]] on Rota's basis conjecture.{{sfn|Pokrovskiy|2018}}{{sfn|Bucić|Kwan|Pokrovskiy|Sudakov|2020}}
His other significant works include a proof with Richard Montgomery and Benny Sudakov of [[Graceful labeling|Ringel's conjecture for large graphs]] and his work with Alp Müyesser giving a random version of the Hall–Paige conjecture.{{sfn|Montgomery|Pokrovskiy|Sudakov|2021}}{{sfn|Müyesser|Pokrovskiy|2025}}

== Awards and honours ==

In 2019, Pokrovskiy shared the [[European Prize in Combinatorics]] with Richard Montgomery. The prize announcement cited their "deep contributions to extremal and probabilistic combinatorics".<ref name="bbk-prize">{{cite journal | journal=Birkbeck International Digest 2019-2020 | title=Prestigious accolades and honours |url=https://www.bbk.ac.uk/documents/international-digest-2019-20.pdf |publisher=Birkbeck, University of London | pages=26–30 |access-date=17 May 2026}}</ref>
